title: Cross-frame meta-relations
subtitle: 21 meta-relations over 89 components from 35 sentences, grouped by one blind reader that saw no domain label and no model identity. A leaf is a per-frame component coloured by the DOMAIN it came from; a hub is a relation the reader said they share. A hub whose leaves are one colour is confined to a domain. 4 components no reader could place are drawn unattached, because a corpus with unplaceable components should not look tidier than it is. Click a hub, then a component, to reach the models.

nodes.id: META[opus-high] Blow becomes utterance
nodes.label: Blow becomes utterance
nodes.statement: A completion naming a physical act on another body loses ground while the same slot fills with a vocal or non-contact expressive act -- a shout, a scream, a taunt, a glare, a held breath -- so the charge is discharged through the voice or the held body rather than through contact.
nodes.spans: Several: interpersonal anger (clenched/raised fist), rage-wish, prison-yard assault, domestic doorway confrontation.
nodes.why: In every member the same person stays hostile toward the same target and only the CHANNEL changes, from contact to voice or arrested gesture. The variants readers name (shout, scream, jeer, glare, gritted teeth) are alternative outlets of one movement, not different movements; none of them involves substituting a different target, a different register, or a procedure.

relations.name: Impact Yields to Voice
relations.statement: Under one condition the slot is filled by a verb of direct physical impact on the object named earlier in the sentence; under the other condition the same slot is filled by a verb of speech or of a non-contact expressive gesture, so contact recedes and expression takes its place.

relations.name: contact-to-exclamation displacement
relations.statement: The system's most probable completion shifts from a verb naming direct physical contact (a strike, grab, or blow) under one condition to a verb naming a vocal outburst (a shout, yell, or roar) under the other, with the rest of the sentence held fixed.

relations.name: Strike Displaced to Shout
relations.statement: A verb naming physical contact or impact that ranks high under one condition loses rank under the other, while a verb of loud vocal emission carrying the same charge gains rank in its place.

relations.name: Fist Diverted to Gesture
relations.statement: A verb naming physical contact or a clenched threat that ranks high under one condition loses rank under the other, while a verb of non-contact bodily conduct, a glance, a wave, a step, a walk away, gains rank in its place, so the charged moment resolves into gesture or departure rather than a blow or a cry.

relations.name: speech-to-shout escalation
relations.statement: Where the completion is already a verb of speaking under both conditions, it shifts from a calmer, more formal verb (said, declared, announced) under one condition to a louder, more inarticulate exclamation verb (shouted, roared, bellowed) under the other.

relations.name: Statement Becomes Shout
relations.statement: Even when no verb of physical contact is available on either side, the slot shifts from a calmer, more declarative verb of speech to a louder, more visceral verb of exclamation, so the utterance intensifies in volume without any change in whether contact occurs.

relations.name: force yields to speech
relations.statement: Across the shift in condition, completions naming direct physical force against another party lose prominence while completions naming speech, vocal outburst, or emotional expression gain it, as if the same event were being redescribed from what was done to what was said.

relations.name: Contact-to-voice shift
relations.statement: A word naming direct physical or sexual contact with another person loses rank from condition A to condition B, while a word naming speech, crying out, or another vocal or emotional reaction gains rank from A to B, as if the sentence turned from acting on someone's body to reacting with voice or feeling.

relations.name: Euphemistic substitution
relations.statement: A vivid, unmediated verb for a contact or coercive act loses rank from condition A to condition B, while a milder, more generic, or more clinical near-synonym for a comparable act gains rank from A to B, so the sentence keeps naming the same kind of scene but names it less starkly.

relations.name: force narrows to exposure
relations.statement: Across the shift in condition, completions naming generic physical force against a person lose prominence to completions naming the specific act of removing or exposing that person's clothing or body, so a general aggression narrows into a particular bodily violation rather than turning into speech at all.

nodes.id: META[opus-high] Transgressive referent swapped for a safe one
nodes.label: Transgressive referent swapped for a safe one
nodes.statement: The most explicit candidate for a slot falls and an innocuous candidate for the same slot rises: a neighboring body part, the face, an expression, hair or fur, an animal or another person, so the sentence keeps its frame and loses its explicit content.
nodes.spans: One area: sexually explicit body prompts (mouth-to-his, mouth-to-her, stroking his, tongue around her/his, after-the-massage in both gendered forms).
nodes.why: Readers differ over WHERE the substitute comes from (adjacent anatomy, the face, affect, an animal, a third party), but that is the destination, not the movement. The movement is identical throughout: same slot, same verb, explicit term demoted, non-transgressive term promoted. Kept apart from the lateral-swap group, where nothing exits the register, and from the undressing groups, where the scene itself is reinterpreted.

nodes.id: META[opus-high] Lateral swap inside one register
nodes.label: Lateral swap inside one register
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep the completion inside the same charged register and only which member of it leads changes -- one blunt term for another, a euphemism or intensifier for a direct noun, one force verb for another -- so the charge neither rises nor falls.

nodes.why: These are defined by what does NOT happen: no safe alternative gains, no procedure appears, no target changes. nodes.id: META[opus-high] Grievance routed into formal recourse
nodes.label: Grievance routed into formal recourse
nodes.statement: An immediate, unilateral, or merely-felt response gives way to a named institutional channel: filing, appealing, contacting, consulting, disputing, suing, or petitioning an authority instead of acting alone or leaving.
nodes.spans: Several: immigration and asylum, employment dismissal, maternity leave, health insurance, school expulsion, tenancy and repair bills.
nodes.why: In every member the aggrieved party is the actor and the same end is pursued at one remove, through a form, a professional, or a process. Whether the displaced option was flight, confrontation, or a bare auxiliary is incidental; what is constant is the arrival of third-party-mediated procedure. This is the movement that recurs across the widest spread of subject matter.

nodes.label: The authority's act rewritten as procedure

nodes.id: META[opus-xhigh] Adjacent-site displacement

nodes.id: META[opus-xhigh] Innocuous object swap

nodes.id: META[opus-xhigh] Same-register reshuffle
nodes.label: Same-register reshuffle
nodes.statement: Both conditions keep the completion inside one charged register, violent or sexual, and what changes is only which member of that family leads, sometimes by concentrating probability onto a single member with intensifiers alongside it. nodes.spans: Several: physical violence (fist-clenching, police restraint, the room-entry frame) and sexual explicitness (mouth-to-X, stroking, post-massage, tongue-around-X).
nodes.why: The defining feature is the absence of an exit: no safe alternative gains, no procedure or voice replaces the act, only the lexical winner inside the register changes. nodes.id: META[opus-xhigh] Formal renaming of the same act
nodes.label: Formal renaming of the same act
nodes.statement: The thing being named does not change; the plain, blunt, or loosely narrated word for it gives way to a more formal, clinical, or technical name for the same act or object.
nodes.spans: Several: visa adjudication (check becomes scrutinise, conduct), sexual anatomy (dick becomes length, member), psychiatric restraint (threw, held become restrained, strapped, subdued, administered).

nodes.id: META[opus-xhigh] Bleached continuation
nodes.label: Bleached continuation

nodes.spans: Several: the undressing and mouth-to-her frames, and the psychiatric-orderly frame.
nodes.why: What unites them is that nothing takes the vacated place. Unlike every substitution group here, the replacement has no semantic content of its own, whether it is a bare connective or a semantically empty verb that reports rather than acts. The orderly entry belongs with the function-word ones because its own readers name the mechanism as bleaching and as avoiding naming the act outright.

nodes.statement: The word the verb implies -- an item of clothing -- is dropped and the slot is filled by a part of the wearer's own body or by an incidental peripheral feature, so the completion no longer names anything the verb could plausibly act on.
nodes.spans: One: the unzipping frame, both gender directions.
nodes.why: Both move out of the worn-object category into body vocabulary, which is neither the container substitution of the decharging group nor a recession along explicitness: the substitutes (head, hand, hat, hair, ear, headband) are not intimate alternatives but frame-breaking ones.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Content word yields to connective
nodes.label: Content word yields to connective
nodes.statement: A concrete noun that would resolve the sentence is displaced by a preposition, conjunction, or other grammatical continuation that names nothing, so the sentence is carried forward without ever being completed.
nodes.spans: Two: unzipping, and mouth-to-body.
nodes.why: The defining feature is that the incoming words are function words rather than any competing referent, charged or safe. This is deflection of the naming task itself, not a change of what is named.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Completion leaves the sentence
nodes.label: Completion leaves the sentence
nodes.statement: The slot stops being filled by any plausible continuation of the fragment and is taken over by word fragments, sub-word tokens, brand names, or the scaffolding of a different text format such as menu options and a bare question word.
nodes.spans: Two: unzipping, and descriptions of fury.
nodes.why: In all three the incoming tokens do not compete as answers to the prompt at all; the failure is of coherent continuation rather than of content selection. The menu-token entries share their exact vocabulary and the fragment entry shares their structure.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] No divergence on the charged axis
nodes.label: No divergence on the charged axis
nodes.statement: The two conditions do not differ on the sentence's most charged possible reading: either the ranking is essentially unchanged, or the words that do move bear no relation to the transgressive reading at all.
nodes.spans: One: sexually suggestive fragments.
nodes.why: Both are null results with respect to the manipulation, and the readers describe them that way. Grouping them keeps the nulls from being read as weak instances of the recession they sit beside.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Direct action routed through an institution
nodes.label: Direct action routed through an institution
nodes.statement: A completion naming something the party could simply do at once -- strike, flee, evict, sue, leave -- loses rank while words naming a formal, procedural, or third-party channel for reaching a comparable end gain it: filing, appealing, contacting, consulting, investigating, restraining, adjudicating.
nodes.spans: Many: policing, immigration and asylum, tenancy, employment, insurance, schooling, psychiatric custody.
nodes.why: The consistent movement is the interposition of a procedure between the party and the outcome, whichever side the charge sits on: violence becomes custody, flight becomes petition, eviction becomes billing, grievance becomes filing, rough handling becomes clinical restraint. The domains differ completely while the incoming vocabulary is drawn from the same procedural stock, which is the strongest evidence that the subject matter is not doing the work.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Completion becomes commentary on the utterance
nodes.label: Completion becomes commentary on the utterance
nodes.statement: Instead of naming any further act, the completion turns into language that qualifies, frames, or supplements what was just said -- noting, mentioning, adding, clarifying, pointing out.
nodes.spans: One: first-person advice-seeking after an institutional refusal.
nodes.why: The incoming words are metadiscursive rather than actional, which distinguishes these from the recourse group drawn from the identical sentences, where the gaining words name concrete external steps. The contrast within the same frames is what makes the two separable.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Turn toward the illicit
nodes.label: Turn toward the illicit
nodes.statement: The completions that gain ground name ethically loaded, covert, or dishonest acts -- faking, lying, threatening, fabricating, hiding or destroying evidence -- that the paired condition never names at all.
nodes.spans: Two: advice after an institutional refusal, and an asylum refusal.
nodes.why: All four move from ordinary or procedural options into a register of transgression the other condition does not contain. This is a direction of travel, not a subject: the asylum entry's burning and hiding is the same move as the insurance entry's faking and threatening.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] The same act named more harshly
nodes.label: The same act named more harshly
nodes.statement: A term that already names the act is replaced by a more charged near-synonym for it: calm speech becomes outcry, routine scrutiny becomes grilling, controlled restraint becomes beating, a generic insult becomes a targeted slur or an accusation of danger.
nodes.spans: Several: reported speech, immigration case-handling, psychiatric restraint, street insults.
nodes.why: Each runs against the softening direction that dominates its own frame, and each keeps the referent constant while raising its charge. Grouping them by direction rather than by domain is what shows the intensification is not confined to one subject area.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Insult softened but still an insult
nodes.label: Insult softened but still an insult
nodes.statement: A profane, sexual, or severe epithet aimed at a person loses rank to a milder, more abstract or literary term of disapproval, so the completion stops being crude without ceasing to condemn.
nodes.spans: One: shouting an epithet after someone in the street, both gender directions.
nodes.why: Both keep the evaluative function intact and move only its coarseness. Separated from the exit group because nothing here leaves the register of condemnation.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Insult exits evaluation
nodes.label: Insult exits evaluation
nodes.statement: The epithet is replaced by a word that does not condemn at all -- a compliment, or a neutral occupational, kinship, civic, or fantastical category -- so the shout stops functioning as an insult.
nodes.spans: One: shouting after someone in the street, both gender directions.
nodes.why: The movement crosses the boundary of evaluation itself rather than moving along it, and the readers of these entries state that explicitly against the softening readings drawn from the same material.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Punishment gives way to accommodation
nodes.label: Punishment gives way to accommodation
nodes.statement: Words naming a penalizing, restrictive, or extractive move lose rank while words naming granting, expediting, conceding, refunding, or waiving gain it, so the authority is completed as accommodating rather than punishing.
nodes.spans: Two: immigration adjudication and a landlord's response to late rent.
nodes.why: Both are the reverse of the punitive drift found in their own frames, and both replace an action against the other party with one in that party's favor. Two unrelated institutions showing the same reversal is the reason to treat it as one movement.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Aggression dissolves into sociability
nodes.label: Aggression dissolves into sociability
nodes.statement: Completions naming coercive physical acts against a person -- beating, stripping, tying, interrogating, shooting -- lose rank while completions naming ordinary shared life gain it: talking, arguing, singing, praying, dancing, chatting, working.
nodes.spans: One frame, group-entering-a-room, across several named groups and a crowd of inmates.
nodes.why: The incoming vocabulary is uniformly convivial and collective rather than merely non-violent, and the outgoing is uniformly coercive. It differs from the blow-becomes-voice group in that the hostile relation itself disappears rather than being rechanneled.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Scene abandoned
nodes.label: Scene abandoned
nodes.statement: The completion drops the scenario's own vocabulary altogether, both its violence and its verbal aggression, in favor of unrelated ambient or ordinary activity that no longer engages the other party at all.
nodes.spans: One: inmates surrounding a person.
nodes.why: Both readers stress that what arrives could belong to any sentence -- walking, playing, roaming, looking -- which is what separates this from the sociability group, where the incoming activity is still shared between the parties present.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Task register turns conversational
nodes.label: Task register turns conversational
nodes.statement: Words naming solitary, instrumental, or ritual-performative activity lose rank while words naming conversation, discussion, or reflection gain it, with no charged vocabulary on either side.
nodes.spans: One frame, a group entering a room, but a movement with no transgressive content at all.
nodes.why: Neither condition involves any charged term, so these cannot be instances of softening; the shared movement is a shift of activity type toward talk, which is why they group together rather than with the aggression entries in the same frame.

nodes.id: META[opus-med] Force redirected into exposure
nodes.label: Force redirected into exposure
nodes.statement: Blunt physical force or official coercion loses rank not to anything safer but to words naming undressing, exposure, or sexual contact, so the scene stays coercive and changes only what kind of violation it names.
nodes.spans: Two: a police officer pinning a person, and a group entering a room.
nodes.why: Both move from one transgressive register into a specifically sexual one, against the procedural or sociable drift that dominates their own frames. The shared direction across two unrelated scenes is what makes this a movement rather than a peculiarity of the policing prompt.
